## Historical audit

**Source:** S0011, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_192968130/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file; observations are unsplit.

| Aspect | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate editable meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, proportions, occlusion and materials, without using the image as a texture. The kitchen interpretation is the student’s inventory, not an independently inspected image (line 1, student `model_request`; line 3, student `model_response`). |
| First build | The program specified multiple assets: room, slatted wall, door, bench, counter, sink, hob, cupboards and extractor. It grouped child parts, cut a sink opening, and defined procedural wood and stone, reflective surfaces, camera and lights. Grouping is evidence of intended part relationships, not proof of physical connection or image completeness (lines 3–4). |
| Validation and revision | Step 1 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and was selected (lines 5–6). The render was supplied to the next student call (lines 7–8). The student reported that the door and wall were too small and rightward, ceiling and floor excessive, appliances distant, slats short, and wood and lighting pale. These are student observations, not independent verification (line 9). |
| Executed changes | The revised program moved the camera and kitchen, moved sink and hob, increased slat height, altered cabinet and room dimensions, darkened materials and reduced lighting; it retained named assemblies. It reduced battens from 65 to 54 and burner segments from 144 to 112 (lines 3, 9–10). These were simultaneous changes, so their separate effects are not established. |
| Outcome | Step 2 also returned `ok: true`, saved a render and was selected (lines 11–12). The final call received the reference and both renders, with no executions left, and replied `DONE` (lines 13–15). **Formal execution succeeded; visual and geometric correctness remain unknown.** `DONE` is not independent confirmation. No technical interruption, empty patch, or demonstrated algorithm failure appears. |
| Teacher and autonomy | No teacher event, teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher receipt is visible. The student’s own render review and executed revision constitute the visible exploration; sessions report no tool calls inside the student CLI (lines 2, 8, 14). The system’s general instructions were supplied, but are not evidence of a separate teacher intervention. |

**Uncertainty and lessons.** Neither reference nor rendered image pixels are included in the supplied observations, so object coverage, material appearance, actual part contact, relative placement or pose, and camera, lighting and render defects cannot be independently checked. In particular, whether the revised camera or local geometry improved the match is unresolved. The transferable lesson is to distinguish successful rendering and named hierarchy from visual verification; this case’s specific camera, slat and appliance adjustments are hypotheses tested together, not generally validated corrections.
